name: 23207-visionchat-3b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1).
architecture: Qwen2.5-VL, bf16: a windowed vision transformer in front of a 36-layer 3B dense decoder with 2 KV heads.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup 30%, no cooldown, bounded at 1000 requests with a 1800 s safety cap.
workload: Single-turn image chat, exactly ONE image per request: guidellm `synthetic_text` (94 prompt tokens, min = max) composed with `synthetic_image` (800x640 JPEG, quality 85, noise content, seed 42), 106 generated tokens per request with EOS ignored (`max_tokens` plus `ignore_eos` on the `vllm_python` backend). Each image is seeded by row index, so every request carries a distinct one. At 800x640 the processor smart-resizes to 812x644 on the 28-pixel grid, so one image is 667 tokens after the 2x2 merge and the engine's own prompt-token count reads well above the declared 94; that is placeholder accounting, not drift.
purpose: A photo question-and-answer assistant on a 3B model, one image per request, 256 concurrent users, single GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line. Every other engine-side value is the default a bare `vllm serve`
# gives; nothing here is tuned and there is no tuned.yaml or tunable.yaml.
model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# ~94 text tokens + ~667 image placeholder tokens + the chat template is under 800 on the wire,
# plus 106 generated. The checkpoint's own window is 128k, which one malformed request could
# reserve; 4096 is the plainest value comfortably above what this workload uses.
max-model-len: 4096
